_comment: Reference gallery policy (#980, M9-J2).
The gallery is the out-of-tree reference extension REPOSITORY: a
third-party-shaped, multi-package project that consumes the same M9
conformance tooling the first-party reference extension does. Its shape
is the proof the issue asks for: the reusable gates
(scripts/check-extension-imports.py, scripts/check-reference-extension.py)
run unmodified against this policy via --policy, which is how CI checks
an external-style repository spanning several extension families.
Namespace lists mirror the product-side policy
(extensions/namespace-policy.json) because the product is the same
repository from the gallery's point of view: an extension may import the
public extension SDK roots and nothing else first-party. If the two
policies ever disagree, that disagreement is the bug.
extension_trees points at the gallery's packages/ directory only. The
gallery root itself (README, tools/, keys/, this file) is repository
furniture, not an extension package, so a bare directory glob over the
gallery would misclassify it. Trees are declared explicitly here rather
than globbed for exactly that reason.
required_artifacts is empty on purpose: the gallery distributes through
the extension catalog (tools/publish.py), which carries each package's
manifest as a sidecar document whose artifact claim describes the built
wheel. A manifest that declared the digest of the very wheel it rides in
could never exist, so catalog-first distribution is the honest shape
here. The first-party reference extension keeps its discover-in-wheel
artifact under the product-side policy.
